source.text: Τότε οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παραλαβόντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον συνήγαγον ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.

records.literal_gloss: Then the soldiers of the governor having taken the Jesus into the praetorium gathered against him whole the cohort.

en.L: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The governor's soldiers then brought Jesus inside the governor's headquarters, and the entire cohort assembled around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Pilate's soldiers took Jesus into the governor's palace. All the soldiers in the unit gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Entonces los soldados del gobernador llevaron a Jesús al pretorio y reunieron alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a toda la cohorte.
es.B: Los soldados del gobernador llevaron entonces a Jesús al interior de la residencia oficial, y toda la cohorte se reunió alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Luego los soldados de Pilato llevaron a Jesús al palacio del gobernador. Todos los soldados de la tropa se reunieron alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Alors les soldats du gouverneur, ayant emmené Jésus dans le prétoire, rassemblèrent autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} toute la cohorte.
fr.B: Les soldats du gouverneur conduisirent alors Jésus dans la résidence du gouverneur, et toute la troupe se rassembla autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Ensuite, les soldats de Pilate ont emmené Jésus dans le palais du gouverneur. Tous les soldats de leur unité se sont rassemblés autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kisha askari wa mkuu wa mkoa walimchukua Yesu ndani ya ikulu, wakakusanya kikosi kizima kumzunguka.
sw.B: Kisha askari wa mkuu wa mkoa walimpeleka Yesu ndani ya ikulu yake, na kikosi kizima kikakusanyika kumzunguka.
sw.R: Kisha askari wa Pilato walimpeleka Yesu ndani ya ikulu ya mkuu wa mkoa. Askari wote wa kikosi hicho wakakusanyika kumzunguka.

vi.L: Bấy giờ các binh lính của quan tổng đốc đem Đức Giê-xu vào dinh tổng đốc và tập hợp cả đội quân quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lính của quan tổng đốc đưa Đức Giê-xu vào trong dinh tổng đốc, rồi gọi cả đội lính đến vây quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi lính của Phi-lát đưa Đức Giê-xu vào dinh quan tổng đốc. Tất cả lính trong đơn vị đều kéo đến vây quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그때 총독의 병사들이 예수를 관정으로 데리고 가서, 온 대대를 그분 주위에 불러 모았다.
ko.B: 그러자 총독의 병사들이 예수를 총독 관저 안으로 끌고 가서, 부대 병사들을 모두 예수 주위에 불러 모았다.
ko.R: 빌라도의 병사들은 예수를 총독이 머무는 관저 안으로 끌고 갔다. 그리고 같은 부대의 병사들이 모두 예수 주위에 모여들었다.

pt.L: Então os soldados do governador, levando Jesus para o pretório, reuniram ao redor {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} toda a coorte.
pt.B: Os soldados do governador levaram Jesus para dentro do quartel do governador, e toda a tropa se reuniu em volta {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Então os soldados de Pilatos levaram Jesus para dentro do palácio do governador. Todos os soldados daquela tropa se juntaram em volta {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ የአገረ ገዡ ወታደሮች ኢየሱስን ወደ ፕራይቶሪዮን ወስደው ጭፍራውን ሁሉ በዙሪያው ሰበሰቡ።
am.B: የአገረ ገዡ ወታደሮችም ኢየሱስን ወደ አገረ ገዡ መኖሪያ ግቢ አስገቡት፤ ጭፍራውም ሁሉ በዙሪያው ተሰበሰበ።
am.R: ከዚያም የጲላጦስ ወታደሮች ኢየሱስን ወደ አገረ ገዡ ቤተ መንግሥት ወሰዱት። በዚያ ክፍለ ጦር ያሉት ወታደሮች ሁሉ በዙሪያው ተሰበሰቡ።

ru.L: Тогда воины наместника, взяв Иисуса в преторий, собрали против {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} всю когорту.
ru.B: Тогда солдаты наместника привели Иисуса в его резиденцию, и вокруг {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} собрался весь отряд.
ru.R: Потом солдаты Пилата отвели Иисуса во дворец наместника. Все солдаты отряда собрались вокруг {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}.

hi.L: तब राज्यपाल के सैनिकों ने यीशु को प्रैटोरियुम में ले जाकर सारी टुकड़ी को उनके चारों ओर इकट्ठा किया।
hi.B: तब राज्यपाल के सैनिक यीशु को राज्यपाल के मुख्यालय के भीतर ले गए, और पूरी टुकड़ी उनके चारों ओर इकट्ठी हो गई।
hi.R: तब पिलातुस के सैनिक यीशु को राज्यपाल के महल में ले गए। उस टुकड़ी के सब सैनिक उनके चारों ओर इकट्ठे हो गए।

uk.L: Тоді воїни намісника, взявши Ісуса до преторії, зібрали біля {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} всю когорту.
uk.B: Тоді воїни намісника відвели Ісуса до резиденції намісника, і довкола {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} зібрався весь загін.
uk.R: Тоді Пилатові воїни повели Ісуса до палацу намісника. Усі воїни загону зібралися довкола {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}.

ja.L: そのとき、総督の兵士たちはイエスをプラエトリウムに連れて行き、イエスの周りに全大隊を呼び集めた。
ja.B: それから総督の兵士たちは、イエスを総督の官邸の中に連れて行き、部隊の全員をイエスの周りに集めた。
ja.R: それから、ピラトの兵士たちは、イエスを総督の住まいの中に連れて行きました。そして、同じ部隊の兵士たちが全員、イエスの周りに集まりました。

decisions.choice: the praetorium: the governor's residence in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Latin word meant a commander's headquarters. In Jerusalem it was most likely Herod's former palace, or perhaps the Antonia fortress beside the temple.

decisions.choice: the cohort: the soldiers on hand
alternatives: a full unit of six hundred
decisions.reason: The word names a Roman unit of up to six hundred men. Matthew may mean all the soldiers present.

decisions.choice: around him: against him, gathered to mock him
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean around or against. The soldiers gather to make sport of him.

decisions.choice: headquarters, cohort (B); palace, unit (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use English words for the Roman terms.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("sont crucifiés", 27:38); speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Matthew and in Mark 15: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, and Readable tells the story in the passé composé. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: le prétoire, la cohorte (L); la résidence du gouverneur, la troupe (B); le palais du gouverneur, leur unité (R)
alternatives: le prétoire, la cohorte at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman terms, which French has borrowed; Balanced and Readable use common words, as the English does and as Mark 15:16 does in French.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on the verbs (walimchukua, kumzunguka); spans on free pronouns and possessives only (yake, wake, chake, naye, mwenyewe)
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb's object prefix -m-, which cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa mkoa (governor); ikulu (praetorium); kikosi (cohort)
decisions.reason: The words used for the same places and people in John 18:3, 18:28 and 19 (meaning decisions m1, m2). "Ikulu" is the official residence of a ruler, which is what the praetorium was. "Yake" in Balanced is the governor's and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on the separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, su, sí, ti); none on pronouns joined to the verb (desnudándolo, crucificarlo) or where Spanish leaves the subject out
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually drops the subject pronoun where English says "he", and a pronoun joined to the verb cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. As in the rest of Matthew; this holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: pretorio, cohorte (L); la residencia oficial, cohorte (B); el palacio del gobernador, la tropa (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Latin words; Balanced says what the building was, as "la residencia del gobernador" in John 18:28, and Readable uses everyday words, as the English does (meaning decisions m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "dinh tổng đốc" for the praetorium; "cả đội quân" (L), "cả đội lính" (B), "tất cả lính trong đơn vị" (R) for the cohort
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:16, the parallel: a modern rank would put a precise size on a unit whose size here is uncertain.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 27:27-44; "그분" (L), "예수" (B, R) in the narrative, with "께서" and -시-; the soldiers, passers-by and leaders speak to and about Jesus with no honorific
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters (style guide, sections 4 and 7). The speakers are hostile; giving him honorifics in their mouths would misrepresent what they say, as in the Korean Mark 15:16-32. The narrator still honours him.

decisions.choice: "관정" (L), "총독 관저" (B, R) for praitorion; "대대" (L), "부대" (B, R) for speira
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 18:28 and Mark 15:16.

decisions.choice: o pretório, a coorte (L); o quartel do governador, a tropa (B); o palácio do governador, aquela tropa (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman terms in their Portuguese forms; Balanced and Readable use everyday words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus in English has nothing to change in Amharic; most such pronouns are verb suffixes in any case (አስገቡት "they brought him in").

decisions.choice: "ፕራይቶሪዮን" (L), "የአገረ ገዡ መኖሪያ ግቢ" (B), "የአገረ ገዡ ቤተ መንግሥት" (R); "ጭፍራ" for the cohort (L, B), "ክፍለ ጦር" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Latin name of the governor's residence, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it was. "ጭፍራ" is a body of soldiers under one command, smaller than an army.

decisions.choice: "преторий", "когорту" (L); "резиденцию", "отряд" (B); "дворец", "отряд" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman terms; Balanced and Readable use Russian words for them, as the English does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; Jesus takes the honorific third person ("उनके")
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide section 7). Respect for Jesus comes from the honorific forms at every level.

decisions.choice: "प्रैटोरियुम" (L), "राज्यपाल का मुख्यालय" (B), "राज्यपाल का महल" (R); the cohort is "टुकड़ी"
decisions.reason: As in the English, Literal keeps the Roman word and Balanced and Readable say what the place was. "पलटन" is kept for the much larger legions of 26:53.

decisions.choice: "преторія", "когорта" (L); "резиденція намісника", "загін" (B); "палац намісника", "загін" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman names; Balanced and Readable say what they were, as the English does and as Mark 15:16 does. The soldiers are "воїни" at every level.

decisions.choice: "プラエトリウム" and "全大隊" (L); "総督の官邸" and "部隊" (B); "総督の住まい" and "同じ部隊" (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Mark 15:16 in Japanese, which tells the same scene. Literal keeps the Latin name and the Roman unit (meaning decisions m1, m2); Balanced and Readable say what they were.

source.text: καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν χλαμύδα κοκκίνην περιέθηκαν αὐτῷ, καὶ πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ κάλαμον ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ γονυπετήσαντες ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ἔλαβον τὸν κάλαμον καὶ ἔτυπτον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having stripped him a robe scarlet they put around him, \v 29 and having woven a crown out of thorns they put on the head of him and a reed in the right of him, and having knelt before him they mocked him saying, Hail, King of the Jews, \v 30 and having spit on him they took the reed and were striking on the head of him.

en.L: And they stripped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and put a scarlet robe around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 29 and having woven a crown out of thorns, they put [it] on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, and a reed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right [hand]; and kneeling before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" \v 30 And they spat on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, took the reed, and kept striking [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.B: They took off {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes and put a scarlet military cloak on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 29 They twisted thorny branches into a crown and set it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, and put a stick in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand. Then they went down on their knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and made fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Hail, King of the Jews!" \v 30 They spat on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and took the stick and beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over the head with it again and again.
en.R: They took off {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes and put a red robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 29 They made a crown out of thorny branches and pushed it onto {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head. They put a stick in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand, like a king's scepter. Then they knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and laughed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "Long live the King of the Jews!" \v 30 They spat on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then they took the stick and kept hitting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the head with it.

es.L: Y, desnudándolo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron encima un manto escarlata, \v 29 y, trenzando una corona de espinas, [la] pusieron sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza, y una caña en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} [mano] derecha; y, arrodillándose delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, se burlaron de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, diciendo: «¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!». \v 30 Y, escupiendo sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, tomaron la caña y golpeaban sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza.
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron la ropa y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron una capa militar de color escarlata. \v 29 Trenzaron unas ramas espinosas en forma de corona y se la colocaron en la cabeza, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron una vara en la mano derecha. Luego se arrodillaron delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y se burlaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!». \v 30 Escupían sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y con la vara {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} golpeaban la cabeza una y otra vez.
es.R: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron la ropa y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron un manto rojo. \v 29 Hicieron una corona con ramas llenas de espinas y se la encajaron en la cabeza. En la mano derecha {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron una vara, como si fuera el cetro de un rey. Después se arrodillaron delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y se reían de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Decían: «¡Viva el Rey de los judíos!». \v 30 Escupían sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Luego tomaron la vara y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pegaban en la cabeza una y otra vez.

fr.L: Et, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant dévêtu, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} mirent un manteau écarlate, \v 29 et, ayant tressé une couronne d’épines, ils [la] posèrent sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête, et un roseau dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} [main] droite ; et, s’agenouillant devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils se moquèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, disant : « Salut, roi des Juifs ! » \v 30 Et, ayant craché sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils prirent le roseau et [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] frappaient sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dévêtirent et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} mirent un manteau militaire écarlate. \v 29 Ils tressèrent une couronne avec des branches épineuses et la posèrent sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête ; ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} mirent aussi un bâton dans la main droite. Puis ils s’agenouillèrent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et se moquèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Vive le roi des Juifs ! » \v 30 Ils crachèrent sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, prirent le bâton et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}en frappèrent à la tête, encore et encore.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont enlevé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont mis un manteau rouge. \v 29 Ils ont fait une couronne avec des branches pleines d’épines et l’ont enfoncée sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont mis un bâton dans la main droite, comme le sceptre d’un roi. Puis ils se sont mis à genoux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et se sont moqués de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils disaient : « Vive le roi des Juifs ! » \v 30 Ils ont craché sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Puis ils ont pris le bâton et n’ont pas arrêté de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} frapper sur la tête.

sw.L: Na wakiisha kumvua [nguo], walimvika vazi jekundu, \v 29 na wakiisha kusuka taji kwa miiba, waliiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, na mwanzi katika [mkono] {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia; na wakipiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, walimdhihaki, wakisema, "Salamu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi!" \v 30 Na wakiisha kumtemea mate, walichukua ule mwanzi, wakawa wakimpiga kichwani.
sw.B: Walimvua nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, wakamvika joho jekundu la kijeshi. \v 29 Wakasokota matawi yenye miiba kuwa taji, wakaiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, wakatia fimbo katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia. Kisha wakapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakamdhihaki, wakisema, "Salamu, ee Mfalme wa Wayahudi!" \v 30 Wakamtemea mate, wakaichukua ile fimbo, wakampiga nayo kichwani tena na tena.
sw.R: Walimvua nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, wakamvika vazi jekundu. \v 29 Wakatengeneza taji kwa matawi yenye miiba, wakaikandamiza juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}. Wakatia fimbo katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia, kama fimbo ya enzi ya mfalme. Kisha wakapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kumcheka. Wakasema, "Mfalme wa Wayahudi aishi milele!" \v 30 Wakamtemea mate. Kisha wakaichukua ile fimbo, wakaendelea kumpiga nayo kichwani.

vi.L: Và họ lột áo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng đỏ thẫm, \v 29 rồi bện một vương miện bằng gai mà đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và [đặt] một cây sậy vào tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; rồi quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà nói: "Kính chào, Vua của người Do Thái!" \v 30 Và họ nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lấy cây sậy và cứ đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ cởi áo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra và khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng nhà binh màu đỏ thẫm. \v 29 Họ bện một vương miện bằng cành gai và đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi đặt một cây gậy vào tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sau đó họ quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà chế nhạo: "Kính chào Vua dân Do Thái!" \v 30 Họ nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi lấy cây gậy đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết lần này đến lần khác.
vi.R: Họ cởi áo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra và khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu đỏ. \v 29 Họ lấy những cành gai bện thành một vương miện và ấn lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ đặt một cây gậy vào tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, giống như cây quyền trượng của vua. Rồi họ quỳ trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và cười nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Vua dân Do Thái vạn tuế!" \v 30 Họ nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi họ lấy cây gậy và cứ đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 옷을 벗기고 주홍색 겉옷을 입혔다. \v 29 그리고 가시로 관을 엮어 그분의 머리에 씌우고, 갈대를 그분의 오른손에 [들렸다]. 그리고 그분 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 조롱하며 말했다. "유대인의 왕, 만세!" \v 30 그리고 그분께 침을 뱉고, 그 갈대를 빼앗아 그분의 머리를 계속 때렸다.
ko.B: 병사들은 예수의 옷을 벗기고 주홍색 군인 망토를 입혔다. \v 29 그리고 가시나무로 관을 엮어 머리에 씌우고, 오른손에 갈대 막대기를 쥐여 주었다. 그러고는 예수 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 조롱하며 말했다. "유대인의 왕 만세!" \v 30 그들은 예수께 침을 뱉고, 그 갈대 막대기를 빼앗아 예수의 머리를 거듭 내리쳤다.
ko.R: 병사들은 예수의 옷을 벗기고 빨간 겉옷을 입혔다. \v 29 그리고 가시 돋친 가지를 엮어서 왕관을 만들어 예수의 머리에 씌웠다. 또 왕이 드는 지팡이처럼 막대기를 예수의 오른손에 쥐여 주었다. 그다음에 예수 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 놀려 댔다. "유대인의 왕 만세!" \v 30 그들은 예수께 침을 뱉었다. 그리고 막대기를 빼앗아 예수의 머리를 계속 때렸다.

pt.L: E, tirando-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} a roupa, puseram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} um manto escarlate, \v 29 e, tecendo uma coroa de espinhos, [a] puseram sobre a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça, e uma cana na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} [mão] direita; e, ajoelhando-se diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, zombavam {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, dizendo: "Salve, Rei dos judeus!" \v 30 E, cuspindo {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, tomaram a cana e batiam [{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}}] na cabeça.
pt.B: Tiraram a roupa {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e lhe puseram um manto militar escarlate. \v 29 Trançaram galhos de espinhos em forma de coroa e a colocaram na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça, e puseram uma vara na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão direita. Depois se ajoelharam diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e zombaram {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}: "Salve, Rei dos judeus!" \v 30 Cuspiram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, pegaram a vara e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} batiam na cabeça sem parar.
pt.R: Eles tiraram a roupa de Jesus e vestiram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} um manto vermelho. \v 29 Fizeram uma coroa de galhos com espinhos e a enfiaram na cabeça {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Puseram uma vara na mão direita {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, como se fosse o cetro de um rei. Depois se ajoelharam na frente {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e riram {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Diziam: "Viva o Rei dos judeus!" \v 30 Cuspiram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Depois pegaram a vara e ficaram batendo com ela na cabeça {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: ገፍፈውም ቀይ ካባ አለበሱት፤ \v 29 ከእሾህም አክሊል ጎንጉነው በራሱ ላይ አደረጉ፤ በቀኝ [እጁ] ደግሞ መቃ አስያዙት፤ በፊቱም ተንበርክከው፦ «የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ሆይ፣ ሰላም ለአንተ!» እያሉ አፌዙበት፤ \v 30 በእርሱም ላይ ተፍተው መቃውን ወሰዱ፤ ራሱንም ይመቱት ነበር።
am.B: ልብሱን አውልቀው ቀይ የወታደር ካባ አለበሱት። \v 29 ከእሾህ ቅርንጫፍ አክሊል ጎንጉነው በራሱ ላይ ደፉለት፤ በቀኝ እጁም በትር አስያዙት። ከዚያም በፊቱ ተንበርክከው፦ «የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ሆይ፣ ሰላም ለአንተ ይሁን!» እያሉ አፌዙበት። \v 30 ተፉበትም፤ በትሩንም ወስደው ደጋግመው ራሱን መቱት።
am.R: ልብሱን አውልቀው ቀይ ካባ አለበሱት። \v 29 ከእሾህ ቅርንጫፍ አክሊል ሠርተው በራሱ ላይ ጫኑበት። እንደ ንጉሥ በትረ መንግሥት በቀኝ እጁ በትር አስያዙት። ከዚያም በፊቱ ተንበርክከው ሳቁበት። እንዲህም አሉ፦ «የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ለዘላለም ይኑር!» \v 30 ተፉበትም። ከዚያም በትሩን ወስደው ራሱን ደጋግመው መቱት።

ru.L: И, раздев {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, надели на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} алый плащ, \v 29 и, сплетя венец из терна, возложили на {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} голову, и трость в {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} правую [руку], и, преклонив колени перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, насмехались над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, говоря: «Здравствуй, Царь Иудейский!» \v 30 И, плюнув на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}, взяли трость и били {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} по голове.
ru.B: Они сняли с {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} одежду и накинули на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} алый воинский плащ. \v 29 Из колючих веток они сплели венец и надели {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} на голову, а в правую руку дали палку. Потом они становились перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} на колени и издевались над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}: «Здравствуй, Царь Иудейский!» \v 30 Они плевали на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}, брали палку и снова и снова били {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} по голове.
ru.R: Они сняли с {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} одежду и надели на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} красный плащ. \v 29 Они сделали венец из колючих веток и надели {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} на голову. В правую руку {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} дали палку, как будто это царский жезл. Потом они становились перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} на колени и смеялись над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Они говорили: «Да здравствует Царь иудеев!» \v 30 Они плевали на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}. Потом брали палку и били {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} по голове.

hi.L: और उन्होंने उनके कपड़े उतारकर उन्हें लाल रंग का चोग़ा पहनाया, \v 29 और काँटों का मुकुट गूँथकर उनके सिर पर रखा, और उनके दाहिने [हाथ] में एक सरकंडा [दिया]; और उनके सामने घुटने टेककर उनका ठट्ठा करते हुए कहने लगे, "हे यहूदियों के राजा, जय हो!" \v 30 और उन पर थूककर उन्होंने वह सरकंडा लिया और [उससे] उनके सिर पर मारते रहे।
hi.B: उन्होंने उनके कपड़े उतारे और उन्हें सैनिकों का लाल चोग़ा पहना दिया। \v 29 फिर उन्होंने काँटेदार डालियों को मोड़कर एक मुकुट बनाया और उनके सिर पर रख दिया, और उनके दाहिने हाथ में एक छड़ी थमा दी। तब वे उनके सामने घुटने टेककर उनका मज़ाक उड़ाने लगे: "हे यहूदियों के राजा, जय हो!" \v 30 उन्होंने उन पर थूका, और वह छड़ी लेकर बार-बार उनके सिर पर मारी।
hi.R: उन्होंने उनके कपड़े उतार दिए और उन्हें एक लाल चोग़ा पहना दिया। \v 29 उन्होंने काँटेदार डालियों से एक मुकुट बनाया और उसे उनके सिर पर दबाकर रख दिया। उन्होंने उनके दाहिने हाथ में एक छड़ी पकड़ा दी, जैसे राजा का राजदंड हो। फिर वे उनके सामने घुटने टेककर उन पर हँसने लगे। वे बोले, "यहूदियों के राजा अमर रहें!" \v 30 उन्होंने उन पर थूका। फिर वह छड़ी लेकर वे उनके सिर पर मारते रहे।

uk.L: І, роздягнувши {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, наділи на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} багряний плащ, \v 29 і, сплівши вінець із терну, поклали [його] на {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} голову, і очеретину в {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} правицю, і, стаючи перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} на коліна, насміхалися з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, кажучи: «Радій, Царю юдеїв!» \v 30 І, плюючи на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, брали очеретину і били [{{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}] по {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} голові.
uk.B: Вони зняли з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} одяг і накинули на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} багряний військовий плащ. \v 29 Вони сплели з колючого терну вінець і поклали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} на голову, а в праву руку дали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} палицю. Потім ставали перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} на коліна й глузували з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}: «Хай живе Цар юдейський!» \v 30 Вони плювали на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, брали палицю і знову й знову били {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} по голові.
uk.R: Вони зняли з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} одяг і вдягли на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} червоний плащ. \v 29 Вони сплели вінець із колючих гілок і натиснули його {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} на голову. Вони дали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} в праву руку палицю, ніби царський жезл. Потім ставали перед {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} на коліна і сміялися з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}. Вони казали: «Хай живе цар юдейського народу!» \v 30 Вони плювали на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}. Потім брали палицю і били {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} по голові.

ja.L: そしてイエス[の衣]を脱がせて、緋色の外套を着せ、\v 29 いばらで冠を編んでその頭に載せ、その右[手]にあしの棒を[持たせた]。そしてイエスの前にひざまずき、あざけって言った。「万歳、ユダヤ人の王よ！」\v 30 そしてイエスにつばを吐きかけ、その棒を取って、イエスの頭をたたき続けた。
ja.B: 兵士たちはイエスの服を脱がせ、緋色の軍用マントを着せた。\v 29 また、いばらの枝で冠を編んでイエスの頭に載せ、右手に棒を持たせた。そしてイエスの前にひざまずき、あざけって言った。「ユダヤ人の王、万歳！」\v 30 さらにイエスにつばを吐きかけ、その棒を取って、何度もイエスの頭をたたいた。
ja.R: 兵士たちはイエスの服を脱がせて、赤いマントを着せました。\v 29 いばらの枝で冠を作って、イエスの頭にかぶせました。また、王さまが持つつえのように、棒をイエスの右手に持たせました。そして、イエスの前にひざまずいて、からかいました。兵士たちは言いました。「ユダヤ人の王さま、ばんざい！」\v 30 兵士たちはイエスにつばを吐きかけました。そして、その棒を取って、イエスの頭を何度もたたきました。

decisions.choice: a scarlet robe: a soldier's red cloak, put on him to mock him as a king
decisions.reason: The word names a short military cloak. Its red color imitated the purple worn by kings; Mark 15:17 calls it purple.

decisions.choice: a crown of thorns and a reed: a mock crown and scepter
decisions.reason: The crown and the reed in his right hand made fun of his claim to be king. Whether the thorns were also meant to hurt, Matthew does not say.

decisions.choice: Hail: the greeting given to an emperor
decisions.reason: Soldiers greeted the emperor with "Hail, Caesar". They use the royal greeting in scorn, as Jesus had said they would mock him (20:19).

decisions.choice: spitting and striking: perhaps Isaiah 50:6
decisions.reason: The servant in Isaiah 50:6 gives his back to those who strike him and does not hide his face from spitting. Matthew does not cite it.

decisions.choice: stick
decisions.reason: The word means a reed or a cane. Balanced and Readable say stick, as for the same word in 27:48.

decisions.choice: Long live; like a king's scepter
decisions.reason: Readable uses a greeting still given to kings and says what the stick stood for.

decisions.choice: Salut, roi des Juifs ! (L); Vive le roi des Juifs ! (B, R); un roseau (L), un bâton (B, R)
alternatives: Salut, roi des Juifs ! at every level
Je te salue, roi des Juifs !
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:17-19 in French. The greeting given to an emperor (m3) is "Vive …" in French acclaim; Literal keeps the plain greeting. "Bâton" for the reed at Balanced and Readable follows the English "stick", here and in 27:48.

decisions.choice: mwanzi (L); fimbo (B, R); kama fimbo ya enzi ya mfalme (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names a reed stalk, which Literal keeps. Balanced and Readable say "fimbo" (a stick), as the English does (rendering decision r-en-1), and Readable's "fimbo ya enzi" is the Swahili word for a king's scepter, so the mockery is plain (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "Salamu" (L), "Salamu, ee" (B); "aishi milele" (R)
decisions.reason: The greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision m3), rendered as in John 19:3: Balanced adds the vocative "ee" of solemn address to a king, and Readable uses "aishi milele" (long may he live).

decisions.choice: caña (L); vara (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names a reed stalk. Balanced and Readable say "vara", a stick, as the English "stick" (rendering decision r-en-1); in Spanish a "vara" is also the staff of an official, so the mock scepter can be seen (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ¡Salve...! (L, B); ¡Viva...! (R)
decisions.reason: The greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision m3). "Salve" is still understood as the old salute to a ruler; Readable uses the cry with which people acclaim a king. As in John 19:3.

decisions.choice: "cây sậy" (L); "cây gậy" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:19: "cây sậy" would suggest a soft grass stem, so Balanced and Readable say "gậy", as the English says "stick"; it stands for a mock scepter (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Kính chào" (L, B); "vạn tuế" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:18: Readable uses the cry with which subjects hailed an emperor, so a new reader hears the mockery of a royal salute.

decisions.choice: "갈대" (L); "갈대 막대기" (B); "막대기" (R); "만세" for chaire at every level; "조롱하다" (L, B), "놀리다" (R) for empaizo, through 27:31 and 27:41
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 15:17-20 and John 19:3: "만세" is the Korean acclamation of a king or emperor (meaning decision), and the reed is a mock scepter.

decisions.choice: [들렸다] (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek lets "put" govern the reed too; Korean needs its own verb for putting something in a hand.

decisions.choice: Salve (L, B); Viva (R); cana (L), vara (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Salve" is the Portuguese greeting to an emperor (m3) and is still understood; "Ave" is Latin. Readable says "Viva o Rei", the cheer still given to kings, as the English Readable says "Long live". "Cana" is the reed itself; Balanced and Readable say "vara", the stick it served as, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ሰላም ለአንተ" (L), "ሰላም ለአንተ ይሁን" (B) for "Hail"
decisions.reason: The soldiers use the ordinary greeting as a mock salute to a king; "ሰላም" is how Amharic greets, and Readable turns it into a royal acclamation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "መቃ" (reed) at Literal; "በትር" (stick, staff) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plant word; Balanced and Readable follow the English in naming what it served as, a mock scepter and then a stick to beat him with.

decisions.choice: "Здравствуй" (L, B); "Да здравствует" (R)
decisions.reason: The greeting given to an emperor; the Synodal "Радуйся" now sounds like a church salutation. Readable uses the cry still raised for a ruler, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "трость" (L); "палку" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means a reed or a cane; Balanced and Readable say stick, as the English does, and as for the same word in 27:48.

decisions.choice: "जय हो" (L, B); "अमर रहें" (R)
decisions.reason: The soldiers use the acclamation given to an emperor (meaning decision m3), not an ordinary greeting, so Hindi uses its acclamation for a king; Readable says "long live", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "багряний плащ" (L, B); "червоний плащ" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew names the red of a soldier's cloak (Mark 15:17 has purple, "пурпур"); "багряний" says scarlet without the old church word "багряниця".

decisions.choice: "Хай живе" (B, R); "Радій" (L)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:18: the greeting given to an emperor sounds in Ukrainian as "Хай живе...", not as an ordinary "Вітаю". Literal keeps "Радій".

decisions.choice: "万歳" (L, B), "ばんざい" (R); "あざける" in kana (L, B), "からかう" (R)
decisions.reason: The royal greeting (meaning decision m3) takes the Japanese cheer for a ruler, as in Mark 15:18 and John 19:3. The verb of mocking keeps one kana spelling, as in 20:19 and Mark 15:20, so the fulfilment of Jesus's words can be heard.

decisions.choice: "緋色の外套" (L), "緋色の軍用マント" (B), "赤いマント" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew names a soldier's short cloak and its scarlet color (meaning decision m1), not Mark's purple, so the wording differs from Mark here on purpose.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν χλαμύδα καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σταυρῶσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And when they had mocked him, they took off him the robe and put on him the garments of him and led away him to crucify.

en.L: And when they had mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took the robe off {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away to crucify [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
en.B: After they had finished mocking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they stripped off the cloak and dressed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes. Then they led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to be crucified.
en.R: When they finished making fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took off the red robe. They put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes back on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a cross.

es.L: Y, cuando se hubieron burlado de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron el manto y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ropas, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron para crucificar[{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}].
es.B: Cuando terminaron de burlarse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron la capa y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vistieron otra vez con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia ropa. Después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sacaron para crucificarlo.
es.R: Cuando terminaron de reírse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron el manto rojo y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} volvieron a poner {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia ropa. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron para matarlo en una cruz.

fr.L: Et, quand ils se furent moqués de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ôtèrent le manteau, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} remirent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent pour [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] crucifier.
fr.B: Quand ils eurent fini de se moquer de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} retirèrent le manteau et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rhabillèrent de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres vêtements. Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifier.
fr.R: Quand ils ont fini de se moquer de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont enlevé le manteau rouge. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont remis {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres vêtements. Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont emmené pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kumdhihaki, walimvua lile vazi, wakamvika mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakamchukua kwenda kumsulubisha.
sw.B: Walipomaliza kumdhihaki, walimvua lile joho, wakamvika tena nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mwenyewe. Kisha wakamtoa nje ili wakamsulubishe.
sw.R: Walipomaliza kumcheka, walimvua lile vazi jekundu, wakamvika tena nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mwenyewe. Kisha wakamchukua ili wakamuue msalabani.

vi.L: Và khi đã chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ cởi áo choàng khỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và mặc áo xống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi để đóng đinh [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}].
vi.B: Chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ lột áo choàng ra và mặc lại quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi họ dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra để đóng đinh.
vi.R: Khi đã chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ cởi áo choàng đỏ ra. Họ mặc lại quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi họ dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi để đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên cây thập tự.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그분을 조롱한 뒤에, 그분에게서 겉옷을 벗기고 그분의 옷을 입혔다. 그리고 십자가에 못 박으려고 그분을 끌고 나갔다.
ko.B: 이렇게 예수를 조롱하고 나서, 망토를 벗기고 예수의 옷을 도로 입혔다. 그리고 십자가에 못 박으려고 예수를 끌고 나갔다.
ko.R: 병사들은 실컷 예수를 놀리고 나서 빨간 겉옷을 벗겼다. 그리고 예수의 옷을 다시 입혔다. 그다음에 십자가에 못 박으려고 예수를 끌고 나갔다.

pt.L: E, depois de zombarem {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, tiraram-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} o manto, vestiram-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} vestes e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram para crucificá-[{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}].
pt.B: Quando terminaram de zombar {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, tiraram-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} o manto e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} vestiram de novo com as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} próprias roupas. Depois {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram para ser crucificado.
pt.R: Quando acabaram de rir {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, tiraram o manto vermelho. Puseram de volta {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} as roupas {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Depois {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram para matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} numa cruz.

am.L: ካፌዙበትም በኋላ ካባውን ገፈፉት፤ ልብሱንም አለበሱት፤ ሊሰቅሉትም ወሰዱት።
am.B: ማፌዛቸውን ከጨረሱ በኋላ ካባውን ገፈፉት፤ የራሱንም ልብስ መልሰው አለበሱት። ከዚያም ሊሰቅሉት ይዘውት ወጡ።
am.R: ካፌዙበት በኋላ ቀዩን ካባ ከላዩ አወለቁ። የራሱን ልብስ መልሰው አለበሱት። ከዚያም በመስቀል ላይ ሊገድሉት ወሰዱት።

ru.L: И когда насмеялись над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, сняли с {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} плащ, и одели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} в {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} одежды, и повели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, чтобы распять.
ru.B: Наиздевавшись над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, они сняли с {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} плащ и снова одели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} в {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} собственную одежду. Потом {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} повели на распятие.
ru.R: Когда они перестали смеяться над {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, они сняли с {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} красный плащ. Они снова надели на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} собственную одежду. Потом они повели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, чтобы казнить на кресте.

hi.L: और जब वे उनका ठट्ठा कर चुके, तो उन्होंने वह चोग़ा उनसे उतारा और उनके कपड़े उन्हें पहनाए, और उन्हें क्रूस पर चढ़ाने के लिए ले गए।
hi.B: जब वे उनका मज़ाक उड़ा चुके, तो उन्होंने चोग़ा उतार लिया और उन्हें फिर से उनके अपने कपड़े पहना दिए। फिर वे उन्हें क्रूस पर चढ़ाने के लिए बाहर ले चले।
hi.R: जब वे उनका मज़ाक उड़ा चुके, तो उन्होंने वह लाल चोग़ा उतार लिया। उन्होंने उन्हें उनके अपने कपड़े फिर से पहना दिए। फिर वे उन्हें क्रूस पर चढ़ाकर मार डालने के लिए ले गए।

uk.L: І коли насміялися з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, зняли з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} плащ і вдягли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} в {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} одяг, і повели {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, щоб розіпʼяти.
uk.B: Коли вони досхочу насміялися з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, то зняли плащ і знову вдягли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} в {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} власний одяг. Потім повели {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} на розпʼяття.
uk.R: Коли вони перестали знущатися з {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, то зняли червоний плащ. Вони знову вдягли на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} власний одяг. Потім вони повели {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, щоб прибити до хреста.

ja.L: そしてイエスをあざけってから、外套をはぎ取って、イエス自身の衣を着せ、十字架につけるためにイエスを連れ出した。
ja.B: こうしてイエスをあざけり終えると、マントをはぎ取り、元の服を着せた。それから、十字架につけるためにイエスを連れ出した。
ja.R: 兵士たちは、イエスをからかい終わると、赤いマントを脱がせました。そして、イエスの服をまた着せました。それから、イエスを十字架につけて殺すために、連れて行きました。

decisions.choice: his garments: his outer clothes
decisions.reason: The word means outer clothing. These are the clothes the soldiers will divide in 27:35.

decisions.choice: led him away to crucify him: the goal of the march
decisions.reason: The phrase states the purpose. The execution was carried out by the same soldiers.

decisions.choice: own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these are his own clothes, not the mock robe.

decisions.choice: "십자가에 못 박다" for stauroo at every level, through Matthew 27
decisions.reason: The word of the Korean John 19:6 and Mark 15:13-27; it already says "nail to a cross", so Readable needs no other wording.

source.text: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ εὗρον ἄνθρωπον Κυρηναῖον ὀνόματι Σίμωνα· τοῦτον ἠγγάρευσαν ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Going out then they found a man of Cyrene by name Simon; this one they compelled that he might carry the cross of him.

en.L: And as they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon; this [man] they compelled to carry {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross.
en.B: On their way out they came across a man from Cyrene named Simon, and they forced him to carry Jesus's cross.
en.R: As they were going out of the city, they met a man named Simon. He was from the city of Cyrene in North Africa. The soldiers forced him to carry Jesus's cross.

es.L: Y, al salir, encontraron a un hombre de Cirene llamado Simón; a este obligaron a cargar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cruz.
es.B: Al salir se encontraron con un hombre de Cirene llamado Simón, y lo forzaron a cargar la cruz de Jesús.
es.R: Cuando iban saliendo de la ciudad, se encontraron con un hombre llamado Simón. Era de la ciudad de Cirene, en el norte de África. Los soldados lo obligaron a cargar la cruz de Jesús.

fr.L: Or, en sortant, ils trouvèrent un homme de Cyrène, nommé Simon ; celui-là, ils le forcèrent à porter {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} croix.
fr.B: En sortant, ils rencontrèrent un homme de Cyrène appelé Simon, et ils l’obligèrent à porter la croix de Jésus.
fr.R: Comme ils sortaient de la ville, ils ont rencontré un homme appelé Simon. Il venait de la ville de Cyrène, en Afrique du Nord. Les soldats l’ont obligé à porter la croix de Jésus.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakitoka, walimkuta mtu wa Kirene, jina lake Simoni; huyu walimlazimisha aubebe msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakitoka, walikutana na mtu mmoja wa Kirene aitwaye Simoni, wakamlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakitoka nje ya mji, walikutana na mtu mmoja aitwaye Simoni. Alikuwa wa mji wa Kirene, kaskazini mwa Afrika. Askari walimlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.

vi.L: Và khi đang đi ra, họ gặp một người Sy-ren tên là Si-môn; họ bắt người này vác cây thập tự của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Trên đường đi ra, họ gặp một người quê ở Sy-ren tên là Si-môn, và họ bắt ông phải vác cây thập tự của Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Khi đi ra khỏi thành, họ gặp một người tên là Si-môn. Ông quê ở thành Sy-ren, một thành ở Bắc Phi. Những người lính bắt ông vác cây thập tự của Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그들이 나가다가 시몬이라는 구레네 사람을 만났다. 그들은 이 사람에게 억지로 그분의 십자가를 지게 했다.
ko.B: 그들은 나가다가 시몬이라는 구레네 사람을 만나, 그에게 억지로 예수의 십자가를 지게 했다.
ko.R: 그들은 성 밖으로 나가다가 시몬이라는 사람을 만났다. 그는 북아프리카의 구레네에서 온 사람이었다. 병사들은 시몬에게 억지로 예수의 십자가를 지고 가게 했다.

pt.L: E, saindo, encontraram um homem cireneu, chamado Simão; a este obrigaram a carregar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cruz.
pt.B: Ao saírem, encontraram um homem de Cirene chamado Simão, e o obrigaram a carregar a cruz de Jesus.
pt.R: Quando estavam saindo da cidade, encontraram um homem chamado Simão. Ele era da cidade de Cirene, no norte da África. Os soldados o obrigaram a carregar a cruz de Jesus.

am.L: ሲወጡም ስምዖን የሚባል የቀሬና ሰው አገኙ፤ ይህንን መስቀሉን ይሸከም ዘንድ አስገደዱት።
am.B: ሲወጡ ስምዖን የሚባል የቀሬና ሰው አገኙ፤ የኢየሱስንም መስቀል እንዲሸከም አስገደዱት።
am.R: ከከተማው ሲወጡ ስምዖን የሚባል ሰው አገኙ። እርሱም በሰሜን አፍሪካ ካለችው ከቀሬና ከተማ የመጣ ነበር። ወታደሮቹ የኢየሱስን መስቀል እንዲሸከም አስገደዱት።

ru.L: Выходя же, они нашли человека из Кирены по имени Симон; его они заставили нести {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} крест.
ru.B: По дороге из города они встретили человека из Кирены по имени Симон и заставили его нести крест Иисуса.
ru.R: Когда они выходили из города, они встретили человека по имени Симон. Он был из города Кирены в Северной Африке. Солдаты заставили его нести крест Иисуса.

hi.L: और बाहर निकलते हुए उन्हें शमौन नाम का एक कुरेनी मनुष्य मिला; उन्होंने उसे बेगार में पकड़ा कि वह उनका क्रूस उठाए।
hi.B: बाहर जाते समय उन्हें कुरेने का शमौन नाम का एक आदमी मिला, और उन्होंने उसे यीशु का क्रूस उठाने के लिए मजबूर किया।
hi.R: जब वे नगर से बाहर जा रहे थे, तब उन्हें शमौन नाम का एक आदमी मिला। वह उत्तरी अफ़्रीका के कुरेने नगर का था। सैनिकों ने उसे यीशु का क्रूस उठाने के लिए मजबूर किया।

uk.L: А, виходячи, знайшли людину, киренянина, на імʼя Симон; цього змусили нести {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} хрест.
uk.B: Виходячи, вони натрапили на чоловіка з Кирени на імʼя Симон і змусили його нести Ісусів хрест.
uk.R: Коли вони виходили з міста, то зустріли чоловіка на імʼя Симон. Він був родом із Кирени в Північній Африці. Воїни змусили його нести Ісусів хрест.

ja.L: さて、出て行くとき、彼らはシモンという名のキレネ人の男を見つけた。この人に、彼らはイエスの十字架を担ぐよう強いた。
ja.B: 出て行く途中で、彼らはシモンという名のキレネ人に出会い、この人に無理やりイエスの十字架を担がせた。
ja.R: 町の外へ出て行くとき、兵士たちはシモンという人に会いました。シモンは、北アフリカのキレネという町の出身でした。兵士たちは、このシモンに無理やりイエスの十字架を担がせました。

decisions.choice: compelled: forced into service, as Roman soldiers could
decisions.reason: Roman soldiers had the right to make a civilian carry a load for them. It is the verb Jesus used in 5:41.

decisions.choice: of Cyrene: from Cyrene, a city in North Africa with a large Jewish community
decisions.reason: Jews from Cyrene had their own synagogue in Jerusalem (Acts 6:9). Simon may have come for the Passover.

decisions.choice: the cross: probably the crossbeam carried by the condemned man
decisions.reason: The condemned man usually carried the crossbeam to the place of execution. John 19:17 says Jesus carried it at first; weakened by the flogging, he could not go on.

decisions.choice: going out: out of the city
decisions.reason: Executions took place outside the city walls (John 19:17, 20; Hebrews 13:12).

decisions.choice: compelled (L); forced (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use the same words as in 5:41, compels and forces.

decisions.choice: of the city; in North Africa; the soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says where they went out from, where Cyrene was, and who forced Simon.

decisions.choice: forcèrent (L); obligèrent (B)
decisions.reason: The same verbs as for the same Greek word in 5:41 in French ("te forcera", "t’oblige"), so that readers can link the two.

decisions.choice: "cây thập tự" for the cross in the story of the crucifixion; "Sy-ren"
alternatives: "thập tự giá", as in Jesus' sayings (10:38; 16:24; 20:19)
decisions.reason: The plain Protestant word the Vietnamese Mark 15 and John 19 use for the cross itself, so the parallel accounts read alike; "Sy-ren" as in Mark 15:21.

decisions.choice: "구레네"; "억지로 ... 지게 하다" for angareuo
decisions.reason: The Protestant name form, as in the Korean Mark 15:21; Roman soldiers could force a man into service (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: um homem cireneu (L); um homem de Cirene (B, R); a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cruz (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek adjective, "cireneu", the form by which Simon is known in Portuguese ("Simão Cireneu"); Balanced and Readable say where he came from. With Simon named just before, "sua cruz" could be read as Simon's own; only Literal keeps it, with the setting, and Balanced and Readable name Jesus, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ቀሬና" for Cyrene
decisions.reason: The established Amharic Bible form of the city's name, used for Simon and again in Acts.

decisions.choice: "его" for Simon (plain), "{{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} крест" for Jesus
decisions.reason: Two pronouns stand side by side; only the one for Jesus takes the span, so the setting also shows whose cross is meant.

decisions.choice: "強いた" (L); "無理やり……担がせた" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the verb of 5:41 in Japanese, so the echo of Jesus's words can be heard (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say it as Mark 15:21 does in Japanese.

source.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Γολγοθᾶ, ὅ ἐστιν Κρανίου Τόπος λεγόμενος, ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πιεῖν οἶνον μετὰ χολῆς μεμιγμένον· καὶ γευσάμενος οὐκ ἠθέλησεν πιεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come to a place called Golgotha, which is of a skull place called, \v 34 they gave him to drink wine with gall mixed; and having tasted not he wanted to drink.

en.L: And coming to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull, \v 34 they gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine mixed with gall to drink; and having tasted [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not willing to drink [it].
en.B: They arrived at a place named Golgotha, a name meaning Place of a Skull. \v 34 They gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine to drink that had gall mixed into it. He tasted it but would not drink it.
en.R: They came to a place called Golgotha. That name means "the Place of the Skull." \v 34 There the soldiers gave Jesus some wine mixed with something bitter. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tasted it, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not drink it.

es.L: Y, llegando a un lugar llamado Gólgota, que es llamado Lugar de la Calavera, \v 34 {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron a beber vino mezclado con hiel; y, después de probar[lo], no quiso beber[lo].
es.B: Llegaron a un lugar llamado Gólgota, nombre que significa Lugar de la Calavera. \v 34 Allí {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron a beber vino mezclado con hiel. Lo probó, pero no quiso beberlo.
es.R: Llegaron a un lugar llamado Gólgota. Ese nombre quiere decir «el Lugar de la Calavera». \v 34 Allí los soldados dieron a Jesús vino mezclado con algo amargo. Cuando lo probó, no quiso beberlo.

fr.L: Et, étant arrivés à un lieu appelé Golgotha, c’est-à-dire Lieu du Crâne, \v 34 ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnèrent à boire du vin mêlé de fiel ; et, l’ayant goûté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne voulut pas [le] boire.
fr.B: Ils arrivèrent à un lieu nommé Golgotha, ce qui veut dire « Lieu du Crâne ». \v 34 Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnèrent à boire du vin mélangé de fiel. Il le goûta, mais refusa de le boire.
fr.R: Ils sont arrivés à un endroit appelé Golgotha. Ce nom veut dire « l’endroit du Crâne ». \v 34 Là, les soldats ont donné à Jésus du vin mélangé avec quelque chose d’amer. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y a goûté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas voulu le boire.

sw.L: Na walipofika mahali paitwapo Golgotha, yaani, panaitwa Mahali pa Fuvu, \v 34 walimpa divai iliyochanganywa na nyongo anywe; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alipoionja, hakutaka kuinywa.
sw.B: Walifika mahali panapoitwa Golgotha, jina lenye maana ya Mahali pa Fuvu. \v 34 Huko walimpa divai iliyochanganywa na nyongo anywe. Alipoionja, alikataa kuinywa.
sw.R: Walifika mahali panapoitwa Golgotha. Jina hilo maana yake ni "Mahali pa Fuvu." \v 34 Huko askari walimpa Yesu divai iliyochanganywa na kitu kichungu. Alipoionja, hakutaka kuinywa.

vi.L: Và đến một nơi gọi là Gô-gô-tha, nghĩa là Nơi Cái Sọ, \v 34 họ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống rượu pha mật đắng; nhưng nếm [rồi], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không chịu uống.
vi.B: Họ đến một nơi gọi là Gô-gô-tha, nghĩa là Nơi Cái Sọ. \v 34 Họ đưa cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống rượu có pha mật đắng. Ngài nếm rồi nhưng không chịu uống.
vi.R: Họ đến một nơi gọi là Gô-gô-tha. Tên ấy có nghĩa là "Cái Sọ". \v 34 Ở đó những người lính đưa cho Đức Giê-xu uống rượu pha với một thứ đắng. Khi nếm thử, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không chịu uống.

ko.L: 그리고 골고다, 곧 해골의 곳이라고 하는 곳에 이르러, \v 34 그들은 쓸개를 탄 포도주를 그분께 마시라고 주었다. 그러나 그분은 맛보시고는 마시려 하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그들은 골고다라는 곳에 이르렀다. 골고다는 해골 터라는 뜻이다. \v 34 그들은 쓸개즙을 섞은 포도주를 예수께 마시라고 주었다. 예수께서는 맛을 보시고는 마시려 하지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 그들은 골고다라는 곳에 이르렀다. 그 이름은 "해골 터"라는 뜻이다. \v 34 거기서 병사들이 쓴 것을 섞은 포도주를 예수께 마시라고 주었다. 예수께서는 맛을 보시고는 마시지 않으셨다.

pt.L: E, chegando a um lugar chamado Gólgota, que quer dizer Lugar da Caveira, \v 34 deram-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} de beber vinho misturado com fel; e, depois de prová-[lo], {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não quis beber.
pt.B: Chegaram a um lugar chamado Gólgota, nome que significa Lugar da Caveira. \v 34 Deram-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} para beber vinho misturado com fel. Ele o provou, mas não quis beber.
pt.R: Eles chegaram a um lugar chamado Gólgota. Esse nome quer dizer "o Lugar da Caveira". \v 34 Ali os soldados deram a Jesus um pouco de vinho misturado com uma coisa amarga. Quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} provou, não quis beber.

am.L: የራስ ቅል ስፍራ ተብሎ ወደሚጠራው፣ ጎልጎታ ወደሚባለው ስፍራ በመጡ ጊዜ፣ \v 34 ከሐሞት ጋር የተቀላቀለ የወይን ጠጅ እንዲጠጣ ሰጡት፤ ቀምሶም ሊጠጣው አልፈለገም።
am.B: ጎልጎታ ወደሚባል ስፍራ ደረሱ፤ ትርጓሜውም የራስ ቅል ስፍራ ማለት ነው። \v 34 ሐሞት የተቀላቀለበት የወይን ጠጅ እንዲጠጣ ሰጡት። እርሱም ቀምሶ ሊጠጣው አልፈለገም።
am.R: ጎልጎታ ወደሚባል ቦታ መጡ። የዚህ ስም ትርጉም «የራስ ቅል ቦታ» ማለት ነው። \v 34 በዚያም ወታደሮቹ መራራ ነገር የተቀላቀለበት የወይን ጠጅ ለኢየሱስ ሰጡት። በቀመሰውም ጊዜ ሊጠጣው አልፈለገም።

ru.L: И, придя на место, называемое Голгофа, что значит Место Черепа, \v 34 дали {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} пить вино, смешанное с желчью; и, попробовав, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не захотел пить.
ru.B: Они пришли на место под названием Голгофа, что значит Место Черепа. \v 34 Там {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} дали выпить вина, смешанного с желчью. Он попробовал, но пить не стал.
ru.R: Они пришли на место, которое называлось Голгофа. Это название значит «Место Черепа.» \v 34 Там солдаты дали Иисусу вина, смешанного с чем-то горьким. Когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} попробовал, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не стал его пить.

hi.L: और गुलगुता नामक स्थान पर, जो खोपड़ी का स्थान कहलाता है, पहुँचकर \v 34 उन्होंने उन्हें पित्त मिला हुआ दाखरस पीने को दिया; और उन्होंने चखकर पीना न चाहा।
hi.B: वे गुलगुता नाम की जगह पर पहुँचे, जिसका अर्थ है खोपड़ी का स्थान। \v 34 उन्होंने उन्हें पीने के लिए दाखरस दिया जिसमें पित्त मिला था। यीशु ने उसे चखा, पर पीना नहीं चाहा।
hi.R: वे गुलगुता नाम की एक जगह पर आए। उस नाम का मतलब है "खोपड़ी की जगह।" \v 34 वहाँ सैनिकों ने यीशु को कुछ कड़वी चीज़ मिला हुआ दाखरस दिया। जब यीशु ने उसे चखा, तो उसे पीना नहीं चाहा।

uk.L: І, прийшовши на місце, що зветься Голгофа, що означає Місце Черепа, \v 34 дали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} пити вино, змішане з жовчю; і, скуштувавши, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не захотів пити.
uk.B: Вони прийшли на місце, що зветься Голгофа, тобто Місце Черепа. \v 34 Там дали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} пити вино, змішане з жовчю. Він скуштував, але не захотів пити.
uk.R: Вони прийшли на місце, яке називалося Голгофа. Ця назва означає «Місце Черепа». \v 34 Там воїни дали Ісусові вина, змішаного з чимось гірким. Він скуштував, але не став пити.

ja.L: そして、ゴルゴタと呼ばれる場所、すなわち頭蓋骨の場所と呼ばれる所に来ると、\v 34 彼らはイエスに、胆汁を混ぜたぶどう酒を飲むように与えた。しかしイエスは味わわれると、飲もうとはされなかった。
ja.B: 一行は、ゴルゴタという所に着いた。頭蓋骨の場所という意味である。\v 34 彼らは苦い胆汁を混ぜたぶどう酒を、イエスに飲ませようと差し出した。イエスはなめてみられたが、飲もうとはされなかった。
ja.R: 兵士たちは、ゴルゴタという所に着きました。この名前は、「どくろの場所」という意味です。\v 34 そこで兵士たちは、苦いものを混ぜたぶどう酒を、イエスに飲ませようとしました。イエスは、それを少し口にされましたが、飲もうとはされませんでした。

decisions.choice: Golgotha: an Aramaic word for skull
decisions.reason: Matthew gives the Aramaic name and then its meaning. Why the place had this name is not known: perhaps from the shape of the rock, or from its use for executions.

decisions.choice: wine mixed with gall: Psalm 69:21 (69:22 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: The psalm says: they gave me gall for food, and for my thirst sour wine to drink. Gall is a bitter substance. Mark 15:23 calls the drink wine mixed with myrrh.

decisions.choice: he would not drink: he tasted it and refused
decisions.reason: The drink may have been meant to dull the pain (Proverbs 31:6), or to add to the mockery with its bitterness. Jesus had said he would not drink wine again until the kingdom (26:29). Matthew does not say why he refused.

decisions.choice: wine, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: sour wine, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "sour wine", closer to the words of Psalm 69. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the soldiers; something bitter
decisions.reason: Readable names who gave the drink and explains gall in plain words.

decisions.choice: Golgotha ... Mahali pa Fuvu (every level)
decisions.reason: Matthew translates the name (meaning decision m1), so each level gives the local name and its meaning, as in John 19:17. "Kalvari" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: Gólgota ... Lugar de la Calavera (every level)
decisions.reason: Matthew translates the name (meaning decision m1), so each level gives the local name and its meaning, as in John 19:17. "Calvario" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: "Gô-gô-tha"; "Nơi Cái Sọ" (L, B), "Cái Sọ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:22 and John 19:17: the name is translated literally; "Đồi Sọ" would add a hill that the Gospels do not mention.

decisions.choice: "mật đắng" (L, B); "một thứ đắng" (R)
decisions.reason: "Gall" is a bitter substance, echoing Psalm 69:21 (meaning decision); Readable says only that it was bitter, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "골고다" at every level; "해골의 곳" (L), "해골 터" (B, R); "쓸개" (L), "쓸개즙" (B), "쓴 것" (R) for chole
decisions.reason: The forms of the Korean John 19:17 and Mark 15:22. chole is a bitter substance, the word of Psalm 69 (meaning decision); Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Lugar da Caveira
decisions.reason: "Caveira" is the everyday Portuguese word for a skull and the name by which the place is known to Brazilian readers; "crânio" sounds anatomical.

decisions.choice: The explanation of the name placed before the name: "የራስ ቅል ስፍራ ተብሎ ወደሚጠራው፣ ጎልጎታ ወደሚባለው ስፍራ"
alternatives: A separate sentence for the explanation, as Balanced
decisions.reason: An Amharic relative clause comes before its noun, so Literal can keep the Greek's one sentence and its "called ... which is called" only by putting the meaning of the name first.

decisions.choice: "Место Черепа"
decisions.reason: The Synodal "Лобное место" is familiar but now means a platform for executions in Moscow; "Место Черепа" says what the name Golgotha means.

decisions.choice: "Місце Черепа"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:22: the Greek says "skull"; "Лобне місце" is the inherited Slavonic phrase and no longer says that to a modern reader.

decisions.choice: "ゴルゴタ", "頭蓋骨の場所" (L, B), "どくろの場所" (R); "胆汁" (L), "苦い胆汁" (B), "苦いもの" (R)
decisions.reason: The place and its meaning are worded as in Mark 15:22. Matthew names gall, the bitter substance of Psalm 69:21 (meaning decision m2), where Mark has myrrh, so the drink differs from Mark on purpose; Readable explains it as the English does.

source.text: σταυρώσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον, καὶ καθήμενοι ἐτήρουν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Having crucified then him they divided the garments of him casting a lot, \v 36 and sitting they were keeping watch over him there.

en.L: And when they had crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they divided {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments among themselves by casting lots, \v 36 and sitting down, they kept watch over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there.
en.B: When they had crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they shared out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes among themselves by drawing lots. \v 36 Then they sat down there and kept guard over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross. Then they threw dice to decide which of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes each of them would get. \v 36 After that, they sat down there to guard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y, habiéndolo crucificado, se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ropas echando suertes, \v 36 y, sentados, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} custodiaban allí.
es.B: Después de crucificarlo, se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa echando suertes. \v 36 Luego se sentaron allí y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vigilaban.
es.R: Los soldados clavaron a Jesús en la cruz. Luego echaron los dados para decidir cuál de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} prendas se llevaría cada uno. \v 36 Después se sentaron allí para vigilarlo.

fr.L: Et, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant crucifié, ils se partagèrent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements en tirant au sort, \v 36 et, s’étant assis, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} gardaient là.
fr.B: Après {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avoir crucifié, ils se partagèrent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements en tirant au sort. \v 36 Puis ils s’assirent là pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} garder.
fr.R: Les soldats ont cloué Jésus sur la croix. Ensuite, ils ont joué aux dés pour savoir lequel d’entre eux prendrait chacun de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements. \v 36 Après cela, ils se sont assis là pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} surveiller.

sw.L: Na wakiisha kumsulubisha, waligawana mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa kutupa kura, \v 36 na wakiketi, walikuwa wakimlinda huko.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kumsulubisha, waligawana nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa kutupa kura. \v 36 Kisha wakaketi pale, wakamlinda.
sw.R: Askari walimpigilia Yesu misumari msalabani. Kisha wakaamua kwa bahati ni nani atachukua kila moja ya nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. \v 36 Baada ya hapo wakaketi pale ili kumlinda.

vi.L: Và khi đã đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ bắt thăm chia nhau áo xống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 36 rồi ngồi đó canh giữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ bắt thăm chia nhau quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 36 Rồi họ ngồi đó canh giữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người lính đóng đinh Đức Giê-xu trên cây thập tự. Rồi họ bắt thăm để định ai được món nào trong quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 36 Sau đó họ ngồi đó để canh giữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분을 십자가에 못 박은 뒤에 제비를 뽑아 그분의 옷을 나누었다. \v 36 그리고 거기 앉아서 그분을 지키고 있었다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 뒤에, 제비를 뽑아 예수의 옷을 나누어 가졌다. \v 36 그리고 거기 앉아서 예수를 지켰다.
ko.R: 병사들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박았다. 그리고 누가 어느 옷을 가질지 제비를 뽑아 예수의 옷을 나누어 가졌다. \v 36 그다음에 거기 앉아서 예수를 지켰다.

pt.L: E, tendo-{{deity_pronoun:o|O}} crucificado, repartiram entre si as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} vestes, lançando sortes, \v 36 e, sentados, {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} vigiavam ali.
pt.B: Depois de {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} crucificarem, repartiram entre si as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} roupas, tirando a sorte. \v 36 Depois se sentaram ali e ficaram de guarda junto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Os soldados pregaram Jesus na cruz. Depois jogaram dados para decidir qual das roupas {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} cada um ia levar. \v 36 Então se sentaram ali para vigiá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.

am.L: ከሰቀሉትም በኋላ ዕጣ እየተጣጣሉ ልብሱን ተከፋፈሉ፤ \v 36 ተቀምጠውም በዚያ ይጠብቁት ነበር።
am.B: ከሰቀሉትም በኋላ ዕጣ ተጣጥለው ልብሶቹን ተከፋፈሉ። \v 36 ከዚያም በዚያ ተቀምጠው ይጠብቁት ጀመር።
am.R: ወታደሮቹ ኢየሱስን በመስቀል ላይ በምስማር ቸነከሩት። ከዚያም እያንዳንዳቸው ከልብሱ የትኛውን እንደሚወስዱ ለመወሰን ዕጣ ተጣጣሉ። \v 36 ከዚያ በኋላ እርሱን ለመጠበቅ በዚያ ተቀመጡ።

ru.L: Распяв же {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, они разделили {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} одежды, бросая жребий, \v 36 и, сидя, стерегли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} там.
ru.B: Распяв {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, они поделили между собой {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} одежду, бросая жребий. \v 36 Потом они сели там и стерегли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.R: Солдаты прибили Иисуса гвоздями к кресту. Потом они бросили жребий, чтобы решить, кому из них какая часть {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} одежды достанется. \v 36 После этого они сели там, чтобы сторожить {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.

hi.L: और उन्हें क्रूस पर चढ़ाकर उन्होंने चिट्ठियाँ डालकर उनके कपड़े आपस में बाँट लिए, \v 36 और वहाँ बैठकर वे उनकी पहरेदारी करने लगे।
hi.B: उन्हें क्रूस पर चढ़ाने के बाद उन्होंने चिट्ठियाँ डालकर उनके कपड़े आपस में बाँट लिए। \v 36 फिर वे वहाँ बैठकर उन पर पहरा देने लगे।
hi.R: सैनिकों ने यीशु को कीलों से क्रूस पर ठोक दिया। फिर उन्होंने पासे फेंककर तय किया कि उनके कौन-से कपड़े किसे मिलेंगे। \v 36 इसके बाद वे वहाँ बैठकर उनकी पहरेदारी करने लगे।

uk.L: А, розіпʼявши {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, поділили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} одяг, кидаючи жереб, \v 36 і, сидячи, стерегли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} там.
uk.B: Розіпʼявши {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, вони поділили між собою {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} одяг, кидаючи жереб. \v 36 Потім сіли там і стерегли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.
uk.R: Воїни прибили Ісуса до хреста. Потім вони кинули жереб, щоб вирішити, кому з них що дістанеться з {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} одягу. \v 36 Після цього вони сіли там, щоб вартувати біля {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}.

ja.L: そしてイエスを十字架につけると、彼らはくじを投げてその衣を分け合い、\v 36 そこに座って、イエスを見張っていた。
ja.B: 彼らはイエスを十字架につけると、くじを引いてその服を分け合った。\v 36 それから、そこに座ってイエスの見張りをした。
ja.R: 兵士たちは、イエスを十字架に釘で打ちつけました。そして、だれがどの服をもらうかをくじ引きで決めて、イエスの服を分けました。\v 36 それから、そこに座って、イエスを見張っていました。

decisions.choice: dividing his garments, casting lots: Psalm 22:18 (22:19 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: The psalm says: they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots. Matthew tells the event in the psalm's words without quoting it.

decisions.choice: no quotation here in the SBLGNT
alternatives: many later manuscripts add: so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, They divided my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the fulfillment of Psalm 22:18 here, in words like John 19:24. The earliest manuscripts do not have it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: dividing the garments: the executioners kept the clothes of the condemned
decisions.reason: The condemned were crucified naked or nearly so, and their clothes went to the soldiers.

decisions.choice: kept watch: guarded him so that no one took him down before he died
decisions.reason: Soldiers stayed by a cross until the condemned man was dead.

decisions.choice: drawing lots (B); threw dice (R)
decisions.reason: Lots were small marked objects thrown to decide by chance. Readable uses a familiar game of chance.

decisions.choice: nailed Jesus to the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says how crucifixion was done; John 20:25 tells of the nail marks in his hands.

decisions.choice: kutupa kura (L, B); kuamua kwa bahati (R)
alternatives: kutupa dadu (R, as the English "threw dice")
decisions.reason: Lots let chance decide who got each garment (meaning decision m1). "Kupiga kura" today usually means to vote, so Literal and Balanced say "kutupa kura" and Readable "decide by chance", as in John 19:24, without naming a game the Greek does not name.

decisions.choice: "bắt thăm" at every level
alternatives: "gieo xúc xắc", as the English Readable "threw dice"
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:24 and John 19:24: "bắt thăm" is the plain word for deciding by lot and keeps the echo of Psalm 22.

decisions.choice: "제비를 뽑다" at every level
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:24 and Mark 15:24, and of Psalm 22 that the verse echoes; Korean readers know the custom.

decisions.choice: "ዕጣ ተጣጣሉ" (they cast lots) at Readable too
decisions.reason: Casting lots is a familiar practice in Amharic and needs no modern substitute; the English Readable's "threw dice" is an English choice.

decisions.choice: "бросили жребий" (R)
decisions.reason: "Бросить жребий" is an everyday Russian phrase for deciding by chance, so Readable keeps it.

decisions.choice: "кинули жереб" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:24: "кидати жереб" is still the ordinary Ukrainian phrase for deciding by lot, so it serves every level where the English Readable says dice.

decisions.choice: "くじを引いて" (B); "くじ引きで決めて" (R)
alternatives: "さいころを振って" as the English Readable's dice
decisions.reason: "くじ" is the familiar Japanese word for deciding by chance and keeps the wording of Psalm 22:18 (meaning decision m1), as in Mark 15:24 in Japanese, so no level needs the English Readable's dice.

source.text: καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένην· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

records.literal_gloss: And they put above the head of him the charge of him having been written: This is Jesus the King of the Jews.

en.L: And above {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head they put up the charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, written: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
en.B: Over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head they placed the charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in writing: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
en.R: Above {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head they put a sign that told why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was being killed. It said, "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."

es.L: Y pusieron sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza la acusación contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, escrita: «Este es Jesús, el Rey de los judíos».
es.B: Encima de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza colocaron por escrito el cargo contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «Este es Jesús, el Rey de los judíos».
es.R: Encima de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza pusieron un letrero que decía por qué {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mataban: «Este es Jesús, el Rey de los judíos».

fr.L: Et ils placèrent au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} accusation, écrite : « Celui-ci est Jésus, le roi des Juifs. »
fr.B: Au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête, ils placèrent par écrit le motif de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} condamnation : « C’est Jésus, le roi des Juifs. »
fr.R: Au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête, ils ont mis un écriteau qui disait pourquoi on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faisait mourir. On y lisait : « C’est Jésus, le roi des Juifs. »

sw.L: Na juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} waliweka shtaka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} lililoandikwa: "Huyu ni Yesu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.B: Juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} waliweka maandishi ya shtaka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: "Huyu ni Yesu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.R: Juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} waliweka kibao kilichoeleza kwa nini alikuwa akiuawa. Kiliandikwa, "Huyu ni Yesu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

vi.L: Và phía trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ đặt bản ghi tội trạng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Đây là Giê-xu, Vua của người Do Thái."
vi.B: Phía trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ treo tấm bảng ghi tội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Đây là Giê-xu, Vua dân Do Thái."
vi.R: Phía trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ treo một tấm bảng cho biết vì sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị xử tử. Trên đó ghi: "Đây là Giê-xu, Vua dân Do Thái."

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 머리 위에 그분의 죄목을 써서 붙였다. "이 사람은 유대인의 왕 예수다."
ko.B: 그리고 예수의 머리 위에 죄목을 적은 죄패를 붙였다. "이 사람은 유대인의 왕 예수다."
ko.R: 그리고 예수의 머리 위에 예수께서 왜 죽임을 당하시는지 알리는 팻말을 붙였다. 거기에는 "이 사람은 유대인의 왕 예수다"라고 쓰여 있었다.

pt.L: E puseram acima da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça a acusação contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, escrita: "Este é Jesus, o Rei dos judeus."
pt.B: Acima da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça puseram por escrito a acusação contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Este é Jesus, o Rei dos judeus."
pt.R: Acima da cabeça {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} puseram uma placa que dizia por que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava sendo morto. Estava escrito: "Este é Jesus, o Rei dos judeus."

am.L: ከራሱም በላይ የተጻፈ ክሱን አኖሩ፦ «ይህ የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ኢየሱስ ነው።»
am.B: ከራሱ በላይ የተከሰሰበትን ጽፈው አኖሩ፦ «ይህ የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ኢየሱስ ነው።»
am.R: ከራሱ በላይ ለምን እንደሚገደል የሚያሳይ ጽሑፍ አኖሩ። ጽሑፉም፦ «ይህ የአይሁድ ንጉሥ ኢየሱስ ነው» ይላል።

ru.L: И поместили над {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} головой написанную вину {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}: «Это Иисус, Царь Иудейский.»
ru.B: Над {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} головой прикрепили надпись с обвинением против {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}: «Это Иисус, Царь Иудейский.»
ru.R: Над {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} головой прибили табличку, на которой было написано, за что {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} казнят. Там было написано: «Это Иисус, Царь иудеев.»

hi.L: और उन्होंने उनके सिर के ऊपर उनका दोषपत्र लिखकर लगाया: "यह यहूदियों का राजा यीशु है।"
hi.B: उनके सिर के ऊपर उन्होंने उनका अभियोग लिखकर लगा दिया: "यह यीशु है, यहूदियों का राजा।"
hi.R: उनके सिर के ऊपर उन्होंने एक तख़्ती लगाई, जिस पर लिखा था कि उन्हें क्यों मारा जा रहा है। उस पर लिखा था, "यह यीशु है, यहूदियों का राजा।"

uk.L: І помістили над {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} головою {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} провину, написану: «Це Ісус, Цар юдеїв.»
uk.B: Над {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} головою прибили письмове звинувачення проти {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}: «Це Ісус, Цар юдейський.»
uk.R: Над {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} головою прибили табличку, на якій було написано, за що {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} стратили. Там було написано: «Це Ісус, цар юдейського народу.»

ja.L: そしてイエスの頭の上に、イエスの罪状を書いたものを掲げた。「これはユダヤ人の王イエスである。」
ja.B: またイエスの頭上には、罪状書きを掲げた。そこには、「これはユダヤ人の王イエスである」と書いてあった。
ja.R: イエスの頭の上には、イエスがなぜ殺されるのかを書いた札が掲げられました。そこには、「これはユダヤ人の王イエスだ」と書いてありました。

decisions.choice: the charge: a written notice of the crime
decisions.reason: A notice giving the crime was often carried before the condemned or fixed to the cross. The charge was claiming to be king, a crime against Rome (27:11).

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: a mocking charge that Matthew presents as true
decisions.reason: Jesus was greeted with this title at his birth (2:2). The Romans wrote it in scorn; Matthew's readers know Jesus is the king it names.

decisions.choice: a sign that told why he was being killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the charge was.

decisions.choice: "Giê-xu" without "Đức" in the written charge
decisions.reason: The notice is the Romans' wording, so the name stands without the honorific, as in the Vietnamese John 19:19.

decisions.choice: "죄목" (L); "죄목을 적은 죄패" (B); "팻말" (R)
decisions.reason: A written notice of the crime (meaning decision), in the words of the Korean Mark 15:26 and John 19:19.

source.text: Τότε σταυροῦνται σὺν αὐτῷ δύο λῃσταί, εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων.

records.literal_gloss: Then are crucified with him two bandits, one on right and one on left.

en.L: Then two bandits are crucified with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, one on [the] right and one on [the] left.
en.B: Two bandits were crucified along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, one at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right and the other at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.
en.R: Two robbers were also killed on crosses next to Jesus. One was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side, and the other was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

es.L: Entonces son crucificados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dos bandidos, uno a [la] derecha y uno a [la] izquierda.
es.B: Con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crucificaron a dos bandidos, uno a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} izquierda.
es.R: A dos ladrones también los clavaron en cruces junto a Jesús. Uno estaba a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} izquierda.

fr.L: Alors sont crucifiés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} deux bandits, un à droite et un à gauche.
fr.B: Deux bandits furent crucifiés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite, l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gauche.
fr.R: Deux voleurs ont aussi été cloués sur des croix à côté de Jésus. L’un était à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite, et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gauche.

sw.L: Kisha wanasulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} wanyang'anyi wawili, mmoja upande wa kulia na mmoja upande wa kushoto.
sw.B: Wanyang'anyi wawili walisulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Wanyang'anyi wawili pia waliuawa msalabani karibu na Yesu. Mmoja alikuwa upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

vi.L: Bấy giờ hai kẻ cướp bị đóng đinh cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, một [kẻ] bên phải và một [kẻ] bên trái.
vi.B: Có hai kẻ cướp cũng bị đóng đinh cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, một kẻ bên phải và một kẻ bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Có hai tên cướp cũng bị đóng đinh trên cây thập tự cạnh Đức Giê-xu, một tên ở bên phải, một tên ở bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그때 강도 두 사람이 그분과 함께 십자가에 못 박힌다. 하나는 오른쪽에, 하나는 왼쪽에 [못 박힌다].
ko.B: 강도 두 사람도 예수와 함께 십자가에 못 박혔는데, 한 사람은 예수의 오른쪽에, 다른 한 사람은 왼쪽에 있었다.
ko.R: 강도 두 사람도 예수 곁에서 십자가에 못 박혔다. 한 사람은 예수의 오른쪽에, 다른 한 사람은 왼쪽에 있었다.

pt.L: Então são crucificados com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dois bandidos, um à direita e um à esquerda.
pt.B: Dois bandidos foram crucificados com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, um à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} direita e o outro à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} esquerda.
pt.R: Dois ladrões também foram mortos em cruzes ao lado de Jesus. Um ficou do lado direito {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, e o outro do lado esquerdo.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜ ሁለት ወንበዴዎች አንዱ በቀኝ አንዱም በግራ ከእርሱ ጋር ይሰቀላሉ።
am.B: ሁለት ወንበዴዎችም አንዱ በቀኙ ሌላው በግራው ከእርሱ ጋር ተሰቀሉ።
am.R: ሁለት ዘራፊዎችም ከኢየሱስ አጠገብ በመስቀሎች ላይ ተሰቅለው ተገደሉ። አንዱ በቀኙ፣ ሌላው በግራው ነበር።

ru.L: Тогда распинают с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} двух разбойников, одного справа и одного слева.
ru.B: Вместе с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} распяли двух разбойников, одного справа от {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}, а другого слева.
ru.R: Рядом с Иисусом распяли ещё двух разбойников. Один был справа от {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}, а другой слева.

hi.L: तब उनके साथ दो डाकू क्रूस पर चढ़ाए जाते हैं, एक दाहिनी ओर और एक बाईं ओर।
hi.B: उनके साथ दो डाकू भी क्रूस पर चढ़ाए गए, एक उनकी दाहिनी ओर और दूसरा बाईं ओर।
hi.R: यीशु के पास दो लुटेरों को भी क्रूस पर चढ़ाकर मारा गया। एक उनकी दाहिनी तरफ़ था और दूसरा बाईं तरफ़।

uk.L: Тоді розпинають з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} двох розбійників, одного праворуч, а одного ліворуч.
uk.B: Разом з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} розіпʼяли двох розбійників, одного праворуч від {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, а другого ліворуч.
uk.R: Поруч з Ісусом прибили до хрестів ще двох грабіжників. Один був праворуч від {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, а другий ліворуч.

ja.L: そのとき、二人の強盗がイエスと一緒に十字架につけられる。一人は右に、一人は左に。
ja.B: そのとき、二人の強盗も、一人はイエスの右に、一人は左に、イエスと一緒に十字架につけられた。
ja.R: そのとき、二人の強盗も、イエスの両側で十字架につけられました。一人はイエスの右側に、もう一人は左側にいました。

decisions.choice: bandits: robbers, or violent rebels
decisions.reason: The word is used of armed robbers and of rebels who took up arms against Rome. It is stronger than thief.

decisions.choice: one on the right and one on the left: perhaps an echo of 20:21
decisions.reason: The mother of Zebedee's sons asked that her sons sit at Jesus's right and left in his kingdom (20:21-23). The places beside the king are now crosses.

decisions.choice: crucified with bandits: perhaps Isaiah 53:12
decisions.reason: The servant in Isaiah 53:12 is counted among wrongdoers. Matthew does not cite the verse.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: robbers
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (wanasulubiwa); past at Balanced and Readable; wanyang'anyi at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's present, as the English Literal does (rendering decision r-en-1). "Mnyang'anyi" is a robber who uses force, as in John 18:40, and can also cover a violent rebel (meaning decision m1); "mwizi" is a sneak thief.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (son crucificados); past at Balanced and Readable (crucificaron, clavaron)
decisions.reason: As the English (rendering decision r-en-1): Literal keeps Matthew's present; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: "kẻ cướp" (L, B); "tên cướp" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 15:27; the meaning decision allows robbers or violent rebels, and "cướp" is the word Jesus used in 26:55.

decisions.choice: "강도" for lestes at every level, here and in 27:44
